entries.name: The New Ultimate Universe
entries.description: Jonathan Hickman's rebuilt Ultimate line in publication-adjacent order, from Ultimate Invasion (2023) through Ultimate Impact: Reborn.

entries.name: The New Ultimate Universe: Collected Editions
entries.description: The same line read the way it is collected, one section per trade paperback, for readers who buy the books rather than the single issues. Each section is a volume you can buy, and it tracks its own progress. Reading is shared with the issue-by-issue order, so an issue ticked in one is ticked in the other. The volume line-up follows Comic Book Herald's collected-edition guide and is not derived from Marvel metadata, which carries no collection records for this era. Six issues Marvel has not collected are left out: the 2024 Free Comic Book Day issue and the five-part Ultimate Impact: Reborn.

entries.name: House of M
entries.description: Wanda Maximoff rewrites the world in Marvel's 2005 event, in publication order: the eight-issue main series, its branded tie-in mini-series, and the Decimation epilogue. Assembled from Marvel series metadata, so it covers the series Marvel branded with the event name and not the House of M chapters published in unbranded ongoing titles such as Wolverine #33-35.

entries.name: X-Men: Silver Age to Claremont
entries.description: The X-Men from their 1963 debut to the year after the Mutant Massacre, in one order: the Lee and Kirby run, Giant-Size X-Men and the Claremont and Cockrum relaunch, the Phoenix, Dark Phoenix and Brood sagas, Days of Future Past, God Loves Man Kills, and the arrival of the New Mutants and X-Factor. Compiled by hand from a reader's outline of Comic Book Herald's guides, read as a reference and re-expressed here, so the order is not derived from Marvel metadata and cannot be checked against it. The Mutant Massacre is read in the crossover's own interleaved order. X-Men #67-93 are left out because all 27 are reprints of issues this order already carries and Marvel holds no metadata for the reprint years. The outline ran out partway through X-Factor's second year, so this stops at X-Factor #23 and reaches neither Fall of the Mutants nor Inferno.
entries.variant: The spine, without the optional reading

entries.name: X-Men: Silver Age to Claremont, with the optional reading
entries.description: The same order as the spine beside it, plus the two sections the outline marked optional. Compiled by hand from the same reader's outline of Comic Book Herald's guides. The Silver Age add-ons are the guest appearances that carried the X-Men through the years their own title was running reprints, scattered across Amazing Adventures, Spider-Man, the Hulk, the Avengers, Captain America, the Defenders and Giant-Size Fantastic Four. The modern retellings revisit the same years from the outside: The Hidden Years, Grand Design, Season One and the whole of First Class. X-Men Annual #1 and #2 are listed without a link, because Marvel's metadata carries that series only from #3.
entries.variant: With the optional add-ons and retellings

entries.name: Civil War: An Avengers Reading List
entries.description: The Avengers path through Civil War and out the other side, compiled by hand from a reader's outline of Comic Book Herald's guide to Avengers trade collections. It pairs the seven-issue event with the New Avengers issues that run alongside it, the Young Avengers and Runaways tie-in, and Warren Ellis and Mike Deodato's Thunderbolts, which is not an Avengers title but is what makes Dark Avengers make sense later. It then follows the split into Mighty Avengers, the Initiative, Avengers/Invaders and the Illuminati.
entries.variant: The Avengers path, through the war and past it
entries.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide
